name: Shaker Style Handcrafted Furniture
old_description: Shaker Style handmade furniture by Master Craftsman Stephen C. Barlow in New Hampshire. American furniture maker and designer since 1989 and proud member of The League of NH Craftsmen. Focused on craftsmanship: furniture thoughtfully designed for functionality, graceful appearance, and a lifetime of use. Shaker Style’s furniture collection of beds, chests, dressers, dining chairs, dining tables, accent table and office furniture are handcrafted with North American hardwood.
about:
Shaker Style Handcrafted Furniture was founded in 1989 by Stephen C. Barlow in Harrisville, New Hampshire. A third-generation New England woodworker, Barlow began the business to continue a family tradition of craftsmanship passed down from his grandfather and great-grandfather. In 1997 his wife Cheryl joined the operation, bringing sales and design experience to what remains a small, family-run workshop. The company is a member of the League of New Hampshire Craftsmen.

The workshop produces a line of Shaker-inspired furniture including beds, chests, dressers, dining chairs, dining tables, accent tables, and office pieces. Each item is handcrafted from North American hardwoods — primarily New England maple, black cherry from the Allegheny Plateau, and walnut from Missouri riverbanks — using traditional joinery such as dovetails and pegged mortise-and-tenon. Finishes are applied in a three-step process: fine sanding, multiple coats of hand-rubbed oil, and a final hand-waxed, buffed surface. The operation is built around made-to-order production rather than volume runs.

Shaker Style sells directly to residential customers and interior designers, shipping finished pieces with an optional white-glove, blanket-wrapped delivery service. The company's client base includes homeowners seeking heirloom-quality furnishings and design professionals specifying custom pieces for residential and small-office projects.

Barlow has stated that the business was founded on the principle that furniture should last for generations, not end up in a landfill. The direct-from-the-maker model, combined with a commitment to sustainably sourced domestic lumber and a durable, repairable oil-wax finish, is presented as the core differentiator.
